body:
Jacob details cars where they sit, mostly around St. Louis, including for a Porsche dealership. The site he had was a Squarespace template that never got finished. The page title still said "Your Site Title". The store sold nothing. The copy read like it came out of a chatbot, because it had.

The problem was not that it looked bad. It was that none of the good stuff was on it. He shoots a foam cannon over a G-Wagon at a stone estate at dusk and none of that footage was anywhere. He has twenty-five five-star reviews and the page showed four testimonials that nobody had written. He details boats, which is in his registered business name, and the site had never mentioned it.

So the rebuild was mostly about getting real material in front of people. The hero is his own 4K footage. The reviews are his actual ones, with names, linked back to where they live. The type is a condensed grotesque that can carry the brand at poster scale, and because the business is called Knock Em Down, the wordmark gets knocked over as you scroll past it.

Built in Astro and hosted for nothing. Every URL the old site published still resolves, so the posts he already ranks for did not go dark. He can add merch and write posts himself through a visual editor that commits to the repo, so nothing routine needs me.
